page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head across the top. A marginal note "Cap.1." in the left margin beside the line "fecundo". Catchword "tis" at the right below the last line.

main_text.l: materiale. Quod oftendit ille lib. de Semi-
ne primo, his verbis. Quando igitur simul
sub idem tempus cum mare femen foemina
emiserit, ipsum muliebre feme per utrunq;
evectum[?] cornu delatumque ad masculi se-
men una cum illo miscetur. Deinde eo-
dem libro secundo de Semine subiungit,
Hippocratis authoritate, ex utrisque mistis
unu fieri femen perfectum. Quod certe a
ratione alienum no est. Quemadmodu enim
alimentum alito corpori assimilatur, ita &
foemineum feme masculo, quoniam huius
illud est alimentum. Proinde Galenus li-
bro primo, de Semine ex utroq; unum fie-
ri declarat. Propterea generationi homi-
nis duo femina neutiquam conveniunt, sed
ex duob. contrarijs, puta foemineo tenuio-
ri, frigidiori & humidiori, masculo crasio-
ri, calidiori & ficciori unum fit temperatu
& prolificum, ac consequenter animatum:
non quod tamen animam actu habeat, sed
duntaxat potentia. Nihil enim actu est ani-
matum, nisi quod iam organicum est, & a-
ctu vivit, quemadmodu animae definitio-
ne nos docet Philosophus, lib. de Anima
secundo. Anima (inquit) est τελέχεια[?], id est,
perfectio corporis organici vitam haben-

page.notes: Running head is printed with abbreviation marks after RER and NATVR; read as "RER." and "NATVR." with doubt. The Greek word after "est" is printed in small type and is read as τελέχεια; the exact spelling is uncertain. "evectum" is read from "eue&um" and is uncertain. The catchword "tis" completes the hyphenated word "haben-" from the last line. Long s is printed as plain s throughout.
